## Summary

This is a Go monorepo (`github.com/usememos/memos`). SSO/identity-provider support lives under `internal/idp/`.

### 1. The abstraction (interface-ish layer)

- **File:** `/bench/home/work/internal/idp/idp.go`
- **Package:** `idp` (import path `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/idp`)

There's no literal Go `interface{...}` type defined here — the abstraction is a shared data type used as the contract's return value across concrete providers:

```go
package idp

type IdentityProviderUserInfo struct {
	Identifier  string
	DisplayName string
	Email       string
	AvatarURL   string
}
```

The real "provider type" abstraction is actually defined in the **protobuf store schema**, which models the provider as a typed enum + oneof config (currently only one variant implemented):

- `/bench/home/work/proto/store/idp.proto` (compiled to `/bench/home/work/proto/gen/store/idp.pb.go`, package `storepb`)

```protobuf
message IdentityProvider {
  int32 id = 1;
  string name = 2;
  enum Type {
    TYPE_UNSPECIFIED = 0;
    OAUTH2 = 1;
  }
  Type type = 3;
  string identifier_filter = 4;
  IdentityProviderConfig config = 5;
  string uid = 6;
}

message IdentityProviderConfig {
  oneof config {
    OAuth2Config oauth2_config = 1;
  }
}
```

There's also `/bench/home/work/proto/api/v1/idp_service.proto` (gRPC-facing API for CRUD on identity providers, compiled into `/bench/home/work/proto/gen/api/v1/idp_service*.go`).

### 2. The concrete protocol implementation (OAuth2)

- **File:** `/bench/home/work/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go`
- **Package:** `oauth2` (import path `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/idp/oauth2`)

```go
// Package oauth2 implements the OAuth2 identity provider integration.
package oauth2

type IdentityProvider struct {
	config *storepb.OAuth2Config
}

func NewIdentityProvider(config *storepb.OAuth2Config) (*IdentityProvider, error) { ... }

func (p *IdentityProvider) ExchangeToken(ctx context.Context, redirectURL, code, codeVerifier string) (string, error) { ... }

func (p *IdentityProvider) UserInfo(ctx context.Context, token string) (*idp.IdentityProviderUserInfo, error) { ... }
```

This is the only concrete protocol implementation present — no SAML or dedicated OIDC package exists yet (OIDC providers are handled generically as OAuth2 with a userinfo endpoint; comments reference "Similar to OIDC's /userinfo endpoint" in `proto/gen/api/v1/auth_service_grpc.pb.go`).

### 3. Where the abstraction and implementation are wired together

- **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go`

This is the dispatch point that would need a `switch`/new branch if another protocol (e.g., SAML) were added:

```go
var userInfo *idp.IdentityProviderUserInfo
if identityProvider.Type == storepb.IdentityProvider_OAUTH2 {
    oauth2IdentityProvider, err := oauth2.NewIdentityProvider(identityProvider.Config.GetOauth2Config())
    ...
    token, err := oauth2IdentityProvider.ExchangeToken(ctx, redirectURI, code, codeVerifier)
    ...
    userInfo, err = oauth2IdentityProvider.UserInfo(ctx, token)
}
```

### Package/directory layout relevant to this feature

```
internal/idp/idp.go              -> package idp (shared UserInfo type / abstraction)
internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go    -> package oauth2 (concrete OAuth2 IdentityProvider impl)
internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2_test.go
proto/store/idp.proto            -> IdentityProvider / IdentityProviderConfig / OAuth2Config messages
proto/api/v1/idp_service.proto   -> gRPC service for managing identity providers
server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go -> resolveSSOIdentity/resolveSSOUser, wires idp abstraction to oauth2 impl
store/ (has store.UserIdentity, store.FindIdentityProvider, etc. for persistence of provider/linkage)
```

Also relevant: `/bench/home/work/docs/plans/2026-04-21-sso-user-identity-linkage/` contains design docs for the SSO user-identity-linkage feature (definition.md, design.md, execution.md, plan.md) if you want background/rationale on this architecture.</result>
